title: Add presubmit lightweight vendoring and phase-aware dependency gardener
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds optional lightweight vendoring for presubmit runs to reduce network flakiness; introduces a phase-aware dependency gardener service that prunes dev-only transitive deps during CI bootstrap to shrink runtime footprint.
description: Context and motivation: Presubmit jobs have become a source of inconsistent CI latency and flakiness due to transient registry/network failures and growing dev-dependency surface (node/python/go). This PR introduces two complementary pieces: 1) a minimal vendoring flow for the presubmit fastpath that materializes a compressed, scrubbed vendor bundle into CI runners when PRESUBMIT_VENDOR=1, and 2) a phase-aware 'dep gardener' service (lightweight CLI) that computes a conservative set of devdeps safe to prune for presubmit bootstraps, based on language manifests and a small corpus of historical bootstraps. Goals: reduce presubmit setup latency variance, avoid pulling large transitive devdeps on every run, and give teams a low-friction opt-in path while preserving full CI for integration/nightly lanes. Summary of changes: - ci/presubmit/bootstrap.go: new vendor-first bootstrap logic and env gate (PRESUBMIT_VENDOR). - scripts/vendor-presubmit.sh: tool that builds the compressed vendor bundle in CI images (keeps archive < 8MB by default). - tools/dep-gardener/main.go: phase-aware pruning algorithm with a small policy config and CLI to generate prune manifests. - ci/manifest/presubmit.yml: wiring to use vendor bundle when present; added a fallback to network install for compatibility. - docs/presubmit.md: updated with opt-in instructions and guidance for maintaining the vendor bundle. - package.json and pyproject.toml: pin a couple dev deps to reduce churn for the vendor bundle; added an opt-in script target (npm run vendor-presubmit / python -m dep_gardener). - test/presubmit/vendoring_test.go and test/dep-gardener/e2e.sh: unit and smoke coverage for the new flow. Design notes and tradeoffs: - Vendoring is opt-in and only used on the fast presubmit lane; full CI (integration, nightly) still uses network installs to ensure coverage. - The vendor bundle intentionally omits large optional tooling (e.g., heavy linters) to keep size small; teams can opt-in per-repo to include extras. - The dep gardener uses a conservative heuristic (manifest-level pruning + historical bootstrap data). It's designed to prefer safety over aggressive pruning; false negatives (not pruning when safe) are acceptable. - Security: vendor bundle generation runs in CI with the same license and SBOM checks; we verify license-check and sha256 before installing. Rollout plan: 1) Experiment opt-in on 10 low-risk repos for two weeks (will enable PRESUBMIT_VENDOR in repo CI). 2) Monitor presubmit setup latency, cache hit-rate, and dependency-related flakes via new telemetry. 3) Gradually expand to more repos after observed stability. Observability and metrics: - Added metrics: presubmit.vendor.cache_hit, presubmit.vendor.bundle_size_bytes, depgardener.prune_rate, presubmit.setup_latency_p50/p95. - Added logs to CI bootstrap for bundle checksums and fallback rationale. Testing performed: - Local unit tests (go/python/ts) and new vendoring unit tests. - Smoke CI lane created (presubmit-smoke) to validate vendor bootstrap across example repos. - Canary rollout on internal/infra and examples/redwood-* repos for 10 days. Related work: ENG-1342 tracked the presubmit flakiness signal; ENG-1375 requested a presubmit optimization for low-latency PR feedback. Links: docs/presubmit.md, Linear ENG-1342, ENG-1375. Checklist: - [x] New bootstrap logic gated behind PRESUBMIT_VENDOR. - [x] Vendor generation script and size guards. - [x] Conservative dep-gardener CLI with policy file. - [x] Unit and smoke tests. - [x] Docs and rollout plan. Caveats and follow-ups: - Need ops runbook to rotate vendor bundles (we add a quarterly auto-regen pipeline). - Future improvements: make dep-gardener incremental; explore repo-specific vendor bundles if needed.
